decisions.rationale: Game 3 decider. Pelipper sets Drizzle, Swampert Mega Evolves and threatens offensive pressure alongside Basculegion and Archaludon in the back against Whimsicott/Ninetales/Gholdengo/Tauros-Blaze core.
decisions.notebook: Opponent brings Whimsicott, Gholdengo, Tauros-Paldea-Blaze, Ninetales-Alola. Drizzle + Swampert/Basculegion/Archaludon handles their speed and defensive veil options.

decisions.rationale: Whimsicott and Gholdengo establish immediate priority weather and offensive pressure against the likely Pelipper–Swampert lead, while Tailwind and Encore punish passive turns or Wide Guard. Blastoise provides a sturdier Mega Swampert answer, and Alolan Ninetales supplies a second weather reset, Aurora Veil, and Freeze-Dry pressure on the opposing Water core.
decisions.notebook: Rain leads are likely Pelipper plus Mega Swampert; prioritize immediate weather denial, speed control, and avoiding reliance on Intimidate alone. Scarf Adaptability Basculegion commonly uses Last Respects repeatedly, so preserve defensive options, deny free targets, and exploit any lock. Mega Swampert is a major endgame threat through Waterfall and Earthquake; retain Blastoise or layered weather control as sturdier counterplay. Gholdengo plus Whimsicott can pressure Wide Guard and punish passive turns with Encore.

selection: Earthquake (all adjacent, including ally Pelipper) + Mega Evolve
decisions.rationale: Tailwind sets up our speed control safely while Mega Swampert uses Earthquake with Mega Evolution to deal major spread damage to Gholdengo and Whimsicott.
decisions.notebook: Drizzle rain is active. Swampert holds Swampertite and outspeeds after Mega Evolving under rain or Tailwind. Keep track of Gholdengo and Whimsicott positioning.

decisions.rationale: Pelipper fainted and must be replaced; sending in Basculegion with Choice Scarf puts immense offensive pressure on Whimsicott and Gholdengo. Swampert-Mega passes its action while Basculegion enters slot a.
decisions.notebook: Swampert holds Swampertite. Basculegion holds Choice Scarf and has Adaptability. Archaludon holds Sitrus Berry and has Stamina. Sun is up from Whimsicott's Sunny Day on turn 1.

selection: Sunny Day (all adjacent, including ally Gholdengo)
decisions.rationale: Prankster Sunny Day immediately replaces Rain, weakening the opposing Water pressure and denying rain-based Mega Swampert plans. Gholdengo’s single-target Thunderbolt reliably OHKOes Pelipper, bypassing Wide Guard; removing its weather and speed-control support is the highest-value opening.
decisions.notebook: Preserve Blastoise and layered weather control for Mega Swampert endgames. Treat Scarf Adaptability Basculegion’s Last Respects as a major threat; exploit Choice locks with Protect, switches, or Encore when safely identified. Gholdengo plus Whimsicott can pressure Wide Guard and punish passive turns.

decisions.rationale: Basculegion outspeeds both foes and uses Last Respects to KO the 10% Gholdengo (which resists Water and might Protect). Mega Swampert uses Earthquake to hit Whimsicott and heavy damage both foes, while Basculegion's Ghost STAB ignores Whimsicott's resist.
decisions.notebook: Swampert has Swampertite. Basculegion has Choice Scarf and Adaptability. Archaludon has Sitrus Berry and Stamina. Gholdengo has Leftovers and Thunderbolt. Whimsicott has Focus Sash and Prankster.

decisions.rationale: Tailwind lets Gholdengo outspeed Scarf Basculegion next turn and preserves Whimsicott’s momentum. Gholdengo must Protect this turn because Basculegion can otherwise KO it with Last Respects; Swampert’s spread pressure is also blocked on Gholdengo.
decisions.notebook: Preserve Blastoise and layered weather control for Mega Swampert endgames. Scarf Adaptability Basculegion’s Last Respects is a major threat; use Protect, switches, or Encore after safely identifying its Choice lock. Whimsicott plus Gholdengo can pressure Wide Guard and punish passive turns.

decisions.rationale: Basculegion is Choice-locked into Last Respects and outspeeds Gholdengo (even under Tailwind), securely finishing off Gholdengo at 17% HP. Swampert uses Protect to shield itself from Whimsicott/potential attacks, positioning us safely into the endgame.
decisions.notebook: Swampert has Swampertite. Basculegion has Choice Scarf and Adaptability. Archaludon has Sitrus Berry and Stamina. Gholdengo has Leftovers. Whimsicott has Focus Sash.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Encore Swampert into its previously used Earthquake while Gholdengo’s Shadow Ball moves first and guarantees the KO on Basculegion. This removes the Choice Scarf threat and preserves the Encore lock for the following turn, despite Swampert still threatening Gholdengo this turn.
decisions.notebook: Basculegion is confirmed Choice Scarf, Adaptability, Adamant, and Choice-locked into Last Respects after using it. Mega Swampert is Adamant with Earthquake, Waterfall, Ice Punch, and Protect; its Earthquake can be Encore-locked after it is used. Preserve Blastoise and layered Sunny Day control for the Mega Swampert endgame.

decisions.rationale: Swampert uses Earthquake to KO Gholdengo and damage Whimsicott, and Archaludon uses Flash Cannon into Gholdengo to secure the KO if EQ high-rolls or Gholdengo protects. Swampert's Protect failed last turn so this turn is safer.
decisions.notebook: Swampert has Swampertite; Basculegion has Choice Scarf and Adaptability; Archaludon has Sitrus Berry and Stamina; Gholdengo has Leftovers; Whimsicott has Focus Sash.

decisions.rationale: Whimsicott should Moonblast Archaludon while Gholdengo uses Shadow Ball into the same target. Encore cannot newly lock Archaludon before it has acted, and Swampert is already Encore-locked into Protect. Focus both attacks to pressure Archaludon before it can exploit the turn.
decisions.notebook: Mega Swampert is Adamant with Earthquake, Waterfall, Ice Punch, and Protect; its Earthquake can be Encore-locked after it is used. Basculegion was confirmed Choice Scarf, Adaptability, and locked into Last Respects after using it. Preserve Blastoise and layered Sunny Day control for the Mega Swampert endgame.

decisions.rationale: Switch Gholdengo to Ninetales-Alola to gain Snow Warning and preserve Blastoise for the Mega Swampert endgame. Whimsicott should remain in place, retaining priority Sunny Day control and its Encore lock pressure while Archaludon is at 3%.
decisions.notebook: Mega Swampert is Adamant, with Earthquake, Waterfall, Ice Punch, and Protect; Earthquake can be Encore-locked. Basculegion was Choice Scarf Adaptability and became locked into Last Respects before fainting. Preserve Blastoise and layered Sunny Day control for the Mega Swampert endgame.

decisions.rationale: Whimsicott has Focus Sash (15% HP) and Ninetales is at 100%. Opponent Tailwind expires this turn. Flash Cannon on Ninetales-Alola is 4x super effective and picks up the KO (or takes down Whimsicott if targeted there; let's hit Ninetales-Alola or Whimsicott). Wait, Swampert Earthquake hits both foes and breaks Whimsicott's sash while dealing heavy damage, while Archaludon Flash Cannon on Ninetales-Alola or Whimsicott secures KOs. Let's use Flash Cannon on Ninetales-Alola and Earthquake.
decisions.notebook: Swampert + Archaludon endgame vs Ninetales + Whimsicott. Whimsicott has sash.

decisions.rationale: Whimsicott’s Moonblast guarantees the KO on Archaludon before either foe can move. Ninetales should then use Freeze-Dry on Mega Swampert for the strongest available damage and a possible KO, while Swampert remains pressured by its Encore-locked Earthquake.
decisions.notebook: Opponent’s Mega Swampert is Adamant with Earthquake, Waterfall, Ice Punch, and Protect; Earthquake can be Encore-locked. Preserve Blastoise and layered Sunny Day control for the Mega Swampert endgame.

reflections.summary: We lost the final game and the series 1-2 when the opponent successfully flipped our rain strategy using Whimsicott's Sunny Day on turn 1, denying Pelipper's Drizzle and empowering Gholdengo while weakening our water attacks. Bringing Pelipper alongside Mega Swampert made us overly reliant on weather, and once the weather was usurped, Alolan Ninetales came in later to set Snowscape, shredding our team with Freeze-Dry under favorable speed tiers.
reflections.adjustment: Against Whimsicott and Alolan Ninetales cores, do not lead Pelipper and Mega Swampert into potential weather-overriding leads. Bring Archaludon and Tsareena or Raichu earlier to pressure Prankster users and block priority, and leave Pelipper behind when the opponent has multiple reliable ways to overwrite rain and punish water types.
reflections.notebook: Opponent favors Whimsicott + Gholdengo leads to instantly disrupt weather with Sunny Day and control speed with Tailwind. Alolan Ninetales serves as a powerful late-game weather setter with Aurora Veil and Freeze-Dry to punish ground and water types. Future prep should prioritize anti-Prankster options and independent damage dealers that do not fold when weather is stolen.

reflections.summary: Won 2-1 because the game plan correctly attacked the opponent’s rain core: Prankster Sunny Day removed Pelipper’s rain, Thunderbolt immediately removed Pelipper, Tailwind enabled the endgame, and Ninetales’ Freeze-Dry finished Mega Swampert. Gholdengo also removed Basculegion and heavily damaged Archaludon, though it was exposed and lost to Flash Cannon. The four brought were broadly appropriate, especially Whimsicott, Gholdengo, and Alolan Ninetales; Mega Blastoise was never used, so choosing it as the Mega slot provided no value in this game. The demonstrated sets were generally well-prepared for the matchup, but there is no supplied evidence identifying a between-game adjustment, so its effect cannot be credited or blamed. Nothing in the evidence proves that Gliscor, Qwilfish, Morpeko, or Meowstic-Female would have been better than the selected six or four.
reflections.adjustment: Keep the Sunny Day, Tailwind, and Ninetales Freeze-Dry structure, but make the Mega choice purposeful: either actively position Mega Blastoise as a rain answer or reconsider spending one of the four slots on it when it is unlikely to enter. Protect Gholdengo from the Archaludon slot rather than relying on it to stay in after securing its early targets. Treat Encore as unreliable when aimed at a Pokémon currently using Protect; do not plan around a successful lock unless the timing is favorable. Against a rematch, expect the opponent to account for Sunny Day and preserve options for controlling weather or punishing Whimsicott.
reflections.notebook: Opponent’s Mega Swampert is Adamant with Earthquake, Waterfall, Ice Punch, and Protect; it can be pressured by Sunny Day and Freeze-Dry, but Encore aimed into Protect did not stop its later Earthquake. Pelipper carries Drizzle, Rain Dance, Tailwind, Hurricane, and Wide Guard, with Damp Rock, so weather and spread-move control are central. Basculegion is Adamant, Adaptability, Choice Scarf, with Wave Crash, Last Respects, Flip Turn, and Aqua Jet; Gholdengo’s Shadow Ball is an effective answer, but preserve Gholdengo from the opposing endgame. Archaludon is Modest with Stamina and Sitrus Berry, carrying Electro Shot, Flash Cannon, Draco Meteor, and Iron Defense; repeated physical hits increase its Defense, while special pressure works better. The successful preparation was layered weather and speed control plus strong special targeting. The main weakness was bringing Mega Blastoise without using or leveraging it; future preparation should either build a concrete Blastoise line or devote that slot to a more immediately relevant option, though the supplied evidence does not establish that any benched Pokémon is superior.
